children: Anthropic, the AI-safety company behind the Claude model family, is reportedly working on enhancing its autonomous Claude agents with built-in negotiating ethics. This development aims to improve the agents' bargaining and dispute resolution capabilities. The report comes as Anthropic is moving towards a confidentially filed IPO, with its recent valuation estimated at $965 billion. Investor discussions suggest potential valuations ranging from $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion. The move is seen as part of Anthropic's strategy to differentiate its agents based on safety and governance attributes while competing at the forefront of autonomous-agent performance.
Market activity suggests Anthropic's development of Claude agents with ethical negotiation skills could lead to a valuation increase.
Current market pricing indicates a 57.5% probability of Anthropic reaching a $2 trillion valuation by December 31, 2026.
The report of Anthropic's ongoing advancements appears supportive of a higher valuation, though the source's credibility is low.

Market participants will be watching for any announcements from Anthropic's leadership, including potential new funding rounds or strategic partnerships with major investors like Amazon and Google. Any significant product advancements or enterprise contracts could further influence market expectations around Anthropic's valuation. Monitoring developments related to Anthropic's IPO filing and subsequent market reactions will be crucial in assessing the company's trajectory toward its valuation targets.

title: FT: Anthropic wants lawyers’ negotiating ethics built into Claude agents that bargain against other agents
